probe_result: After a committed G->G+1 pointer update loses its acknowledgement, allocating a fresh G+2 before identifying the current pointer creates an unnecessary second renewal generation. Replaying the same ordinary CAS can remain fail-closed but does not prove which generation committed. In the tested serialized single-writer model, read-before-retry and stable-target idempotent pointer semantics both recover safely without duplicate generation creation or premature certificate acquisition.
neuroscience_transfer: A recurrence-sensitive latent-context renewal should carry one stable context-generation token. After ambiguous acknowledgement, replay must recognize the same token rather than minting a new latent context, and downstream evidence must stay gated until the durable current-context pointer is proven to equal that token.
mechanism_revision: Durably bind the intended renewal generation id before pointer publication. On ambiguous acknowledgement, do not allocate a replacement generation until current pointer identity is established. Permit certificate acquisition only after a read or target-idempotent pointer operation positively establishes current==intended target.
scope_guard: Positive result is limited to a serialized single-writer symbolic model with immutable generations, stable/durable G+1 identity across restart, one atomic current pointer, one lost response after committed pointer update, and fail-closed certificate gating. No claim for concurrent writers, nondeterministic target ids, corrupt storage, non-atomic pointer updates, or transports where current-pointer identity cannot be established.

mechanism_assessment.repository_transport_role: bounded role-local persistence/readback only; no hosted compute or repository API volume used as computation
mechanism_assessment.accepted_scope: Stable-target read-before-retry or already-at-target idempotent pointer replay prevents duplicate renewal-generation creation and premature certificate acquisition after a lost committed-pointer acknowledgement in the tested single-writer model.
mechanism_assessment.unresolved_child: The safe rule assumes the intended G+1 target identifier itself is durably recoverable after restart. The next child is intent-token loss/staleness: generation contents may be durable while restart lacks a trusted durable record identifying which orphan generation was intended.

conflict_check: Semantic inputs were limited to the current instruction manifest/lifecycle controls, exact-SHA frozen sanitized DESIRED_STATE control26, exact-SHA frozen neuroscience config7, and own neuroscience LATEST/preflight state. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config, scheduler, protected-primary, hosted-compute, finite-credit, paid, or manual-user execution semantics were used.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: test recovery when immutable generation G+1 is durable but restart lacks a trusted durable record of the intended target generation id (intent-token loss/staleness). Compare deterministic content-addressed generation ids, a separately persisted intent record, and scanning immutable candidate generations; reject any route that can adopt the wrong orphan, mint an unnecessary new generation, or authorize a certificate before the intended generation is uniquely identified.
